items.title: Cohomology of a site equals cohomology of a bigger site under the comparison hypotheses
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section comparing a site with a bigger one

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma transfers cohomology from a site D to a site C along a comparison functor u satisfying the hypotheses of the standard comparison lemma, giving RGamma(C, g^{-1}F) = RGamma(D, F), its local form RGamma(U, g^{-1}F) = RGamma(u(U), F) and the resulting H^p identifications, functorially in F (statement lines 653-666). The proof is short but its one substantive point is that the reduction to preservation of injectives is legitimate: degree zero is the hypothesis of the comparison lemma, and the injective preservation comes from the adjoint-pair criterion whose input is exactness of the left adjoint g_! = f^{-1}, which has to be identified correctly (proof lines 670-678). The claim is H2: two cited inputs assembled in the right order, with the local statement following formally.
